fixes.explanation: Paul doesn't narrow it down like that, friend. He says "…all things were created…" in Him, and he lists "…things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible…" (Colossians 1:16). That's way more than creatures. Paul's list is wide: heaven, earth, seen and unseen.

Yes, baker. Paul says the Son "…is before all things, and in Him all things hold together." (Colossians 1:17). Both halves are in the same verse. The Son comes first, and in Him all things hold together.
Not this time, baker. Paul says "…God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him…" (Colossians 1:19). All of it, with no part held back. So "only part" doesn't match what Paul wrote.

The law at Sinai is a fair guess, friend, but Paul doesn't point there for this peace. He says God reconciles all things "…by making peace through the blood of His cross." (Colossians 1:20). The peace he names is through the cross.
Paul doesn't point there in this verse, friend. He says the peace is made "…through the blood of His cross." (Colossians 1:20). That's the way he names, and he doesn't list another.

That's right, baker. Paul says "…He has reconciled you by Christ’s physical body through death to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence…" (Colossians 1:22). Three words, and each one is good news. Paul says it, so I'll say it loud.

Fair guess, friend, but Paul doesn't name the law here. He says not to be moved "…from the hope of the gospel you heard…" (Colossians 1:23). The gospel is what they heard, so that's what he says to hold onto.

That's right, baker. Paul says the gospel "…has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven, and of which I, Paul, have become a servant." (Colossians 1:23). Paul is a servant, and he says so himself. I think that's a humble way to put it.
